subject: general
question: The term ‘bishop’ is associated with which game?
solution:
The correct answer is __**chess**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'bishop'** is associated with the game of **chess**.
 
• In chess, the bishop is a piece that moves diagonally across the board.
 
• Each player starts with two bishops, one on a light square and one on a dark square.
 
• The bishop can move any number of squares diagonally, but cannot jump over other pieces.
 
• The bishop is considered a minor piece in the game of chess, alongside the knight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chess is a two-player strategy board game played on an 8x8 grid.
 
• Each player begins with 16 pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two knights, two bishops, and eight pawns.
 
• The objective of chess is to checkmate the opponent's king, putting it under threat of capture with no legal moves to escape.
 
• Chess is believed to have originated in India during the Gupta Empire, where it was known as Chaturanga.
 
• The modern rules of chess were standardized in the 19th century.
